name: GitOps Workflow
description: Enforces GitOps patterns where Git is the single source of truth for infrastructure and deployments.
content:
# GitOps Workflow Rules

- Git is the single source of truth — the desired state of all environments is defined in Git repositories
- Use declarative configuration — describe WHAT the system should look like, not HOW to get there
- Automate deployments from Git — use Argo CD, Flux, or similar operators to sync cluster state to Git
- Separate application code from deployment config — app repo for code, config repo for manifests
- Use pull-based deployment — the cluster pulls desired state from Git, don't push changes to clusters
- All changes go through pull requests — even emergency fixes must be committed to Git and synced
- Use environment branches or directory-based promotion — `environments/staging/`, `environments/production/`
- Implement automated rollback — if health checks fail after sync, revert to the previous Git commit automatically
- Use sealed secrets or external secrets operators — never store plain secrets in Git, even in private repos
- Monitor sync status — alert when the actual state drifts from the desired state in Git
- Use image tag automation — update manifests automatically when new container images are built
- Audit deployments through Git history — `git log` shows who changed what, when, and why for every deployment
